concepts.definition: The same order in both the line task and the wall task: read the measurement, work out the error, find the PID output, give it to the motors.
concepts.example: On the line the error is the array position, at the wall it is mesafe - HEDEF; the rest of the code is the same.
concepts.pitfall: Using the same Kp for the line and the wall; the error units are different.

concepts.definition: Comparing two methods on the same track, with the same TABAN and the same measurement method, over more than one run.
concepts.example: Running PID and bang-bang at full speed on the hard and the easy track.
concepts.pitfall: Deciding from a single run; noise and the starting point can change the result.

concepts.definition: Bang-bang's dependence on its fixed turn value; with a small value it cannot take the bend.
concepts.example: Of the four turn values, only 200 finished the track.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking bang-bang needs no tuning; the turn value has to be tuned too.

concepts.definition: The average change, at each measurement step, in the speed difference between the left and right wheels; if it is large, the steering keeps wiggling.
concepts.example: On the hard track PID gave a jitter of 0.91 and bang-bang 0.46.
concepts.pitfall: Automatically treating staying close to the line as smooth driving; PID was closer to the line but wiggled the steering more.

concepts.term: I and D on the line array
concepts.definition: Because the array measures in steps of 0.5 and the line can disappear between sensors, it feeds fake jumps into I and D; here Ki = 0 and Kd is small.
concepts.example: When Ki = 1 was switched on, the lap on the hard track got longer, from 8.62 s to 9.40 s.
concepts.pitfall: Increasing Kd by intuition; on the line array the derivative behaves like noise.

concepts.definition: The accepted range of deviation in wall following; here ±2 cm around the target.
concepts.example: After the 4th second the robot stayed inside the band 100% of the time.
concepts.pitfall: Counting the deviation in the first seconds as a failure of the controller when the starting distance is outside the band.

quiz.prompt: In the PID wall follower, KP = 16, KI = 1, KD = 4, TABAN = 170, UMAX = 100. In one round e = 3 cm, integral = 2 and turevSuz = 5 cm/s. What value is given to the left wheel (TABAN - u)?
quiz.explanation: u = 16 x 3 + 1 x 2 + 4 x 5 = 48 + 2 + 20 = 70. Because it stays within the UMAX = 100 limit, u is used as it is and the left wheel gets 170 - 70 = 100.

quiz.prompt: On a track, the PID lap took 9.0 s and the bang-bang lap took 10.0 s. By what percentage was the PID lap shorter than the bang-bang time?
quiz.explanation: The difference is 10.0 - 9.0 = 1.0 s, and its ratio to the bang-bang time is 1.0 / 10.0 = 10%. If you divided the difference by the PID time (9.0), you would get 11.1%; a comparison must say which method it is relative to.

Because A3 and A4 see the line, the line is on the right and yon = -1. Left = 255 + 200 = 455, and constrain squeezes this to 255; right = 255 - 200 = 55. Because the right wheel slows down, the robot turns right.

quiz.prompt: When Ki = 1 was switched on in the line follower, the lap on the hard track got longer and the steering jitter increased. What is the real reason?
options: Ki always makes the lap longer
The array's measurement in steps of 0.5 and the jumps when the line is lost create fake build-up in the integral
Ki only works in wall following
Never limiting the integral causes a compile error
quiz.explanation: While the line passes between two sensors, the error jumps and the integral accumulates this fake error. Ki was useful in wall following, so it is not always harmful; the ILIM limit does not cause a compile error either.

options: The UMAX limit should be removed
The left wheel should get TABAN + u
The sign of e = HEDEF - mesafe is reversed; when moving away from the wall e becomes negative and the robot turns right
The servo should look at 0 degrees instead of 180
quiz.explanation: Our rule was e = mesafe - HEDEF: when far from the wall (e > 0), the robot should turn left, towards the wall. With the sign reversed, e becomes negative and the robot turns right, away from the wall. The wheel formula and UMAX are correct.
